findings.title: Refund route missing requireAdmin: any logged-in user can refund any paid order
findings.explanation: The PR says this endpoint is for admins/support, but POST /orders/:id/refund is registered with only `requireUser`. The neighbouring cancel route uses `requireUser, requireAdmin`. refundOrder does not check roles or ownership either: it looks up the order by id with no `order.userId` check (unlike getOrder), and then calls queueRefund for the remaining balance. So any authenticated user can trigger a full refund on any paid order, including other customers' orders, just by guessing or listing order ids. That is a direct way to lose money.
findings.reasoningSummary: The route registration leaves out the requireAdmin middleware that the cancel route uses, and the handler does no authorization of its own, so any authenticated user can issue refunds.
findings.suggestedFix: Register the route as `router.post("/orders/:id/refund", requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder);`.

findings.suggestedFix: Register the route as `router.post("/orders/:id/refund", requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder);`.

findings.title: Refund routes lack requireAdmin; any authenticated user can refund any order
findings.explanation: The PR is meant to let admins refund orders, but both new routes (`/orders/:id/refund` and the alias `/refunds/:id`) are registered only with `requireUser`. Unlike `/orders/:id/cancel`, which uses `requireUser, requireAdmin`, these routes don't check for an admin. `refundOrder` also never checks that the order belongs to the caller, unlike `getOrder`, which checks `order.userId !== req.user!.id`. As a result, any logged-in user can POST to either path with any paid order's id. That queues a full refund through `queueRefund` and marks the order refunded, which causes direct financial loss.
findings.reasoningSummary: Both new refund routes are missing the requireAdmin middleware that the comparable admin route (cancel) uses, and the handler has no ownership or role check.
findings.suggestedFix: Register both routes with `requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder`, the same way as the cancel route.

findings.title: Legacy /refunds/:id alias skips requireAdmin, so any logged-in user can refund any order
findings.explanation: The new admin-only route `/orders/:id/refund` uses `requireUser, requireAdmin`. The legacy alias `/refunds/:id` uses only `requireUser`. `refundOrder` does not check ownership or admin status. It looks up any order by id, calls `queueRefund` for the remaining amount and marks the order refunded. So any logged-in non-admin user can POST /refunds/<any order id> and trigger a full refund of any paid order, including other users' orders. That is direct money loss, and it gets around the admin-only design the PR describes.
findings.reasoningSummary: The alias route is registered without the requireAdmin middleware, and the handler has no authorization check of its own.
findings.suggestedFix: Register the alias as `router.post("/refunds/:id", requireUser, requireAdmin, refundOrder);`, or do the admin check inside refundOrder so every route to it is protected.

findings.title: Support reopen endpoint missing requireAdmin: any user can flip any cancelled order back to paid
findings.explanation: POST /support/orders/:id/reopen is guarded only by `requireUser`, and `reopenOrder` has no admin or ownership check. Any authenticated user can set any cancelled order (their own or someone else's) to `paid`, which per the comment means it ships again. Cancelling an order requires admin, so this undoes an admin-only action without admin rights. Also, `cancelOrder` doesn't check status, so an order can be cancelled after a refund. Reopening it then gives `status = "paid"` with `refundedCents == totalCents`: an order that ships even though the money was returned.
findings.reasoningSummary: The new support route has only requireUser and changes order status with no authz check, bypassing the admin-only cancel workflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `requireAdmin` to the route, and refuse to reopen orders where refundedCents > 0.
